BOOK_A.title: Status of Counterclaim
BOOK_A.defined_terms: 3.60 ( application of Rules);9.10 (judgment on counterclaim) Though a counterclaim may to some extent adopt the facts in the statement of defence, still it is a distinct pleading and must comply with the Rules requiring that a pleading set out the fundamental allegations. Some counterclaims will expressly incorporate the words in the statement of defence, and if so, both those pleadings must be considered for jurisdiction purposes. The previous Rules contemplated that the counterclaim would be tried with the claim, unless they were severed.The criteria for doing that were not technical, but practical and somewhat flexible. If the two claims are linked, as where the defendant claims set-off, then the counterclaim should not be tried separately. The position is less clear now that a counterclaim isan "independent action".If a set-off is claimed under R.3.59, it will still often be convenient to try them together if they are related.Though the Rules say a counterclaim is a separate action, it and the main claim are not treated as unrelated for all purposes.The grounds for security in the Rules are not exhaustive. A plaintiff who sues in Alberta attorns to the jurisdiction and becomes subject to a counterclaim. The court refused to sever or stay the counterclaim on grounds of inappropriate forum. If a foreign company sues here, our courts have jurisdiction to hear a counterclaim against it, and service on the solicitors for the plaintiff (defendant by counterclaim) is fit service within the jurisdiction. Where one side gets partial summary judgment but there is a pending counterclaim from the other side, the test for whether to stay execution on that one judgment until the counterclaim is decided, is like the test for a stay pending trial or pending appeal. 4Richardson v. There is an extended discussion and citation of authority on the subject of what to do with 1Condo.Plan 8222909 v.Belas,infra. 2Condo.Plan 8222909 v.Belas(M) 2015 ABQB 751, JCE 1203 12256 (Nov 26).See alsoCondo.Corp. # *0213865 v. Uhrik(M) 2014 ABQB 478, 595 AR 141. 3Castle Bldg.Centres Grp. v.Alta. Drywall2023 ABKB 32, JCE 1803 04770 (Jan 18). and whether there is set-off. a counterclaim or cross-claim where the plaintiff gets summary judgment on the main claim. It was made easier in one case because there is no irreparable harm from letting the counterclaim come along later, and the case for the counterclaim was not really arguable. If a counterclaim is pled directly as a defence to the statement of claim, it is inconsistency to decide that the plaintiff can get judgment, yet that the counterclaim as a defence to the statement of claim, can continue. The Court of King's Bench justice left the counterclaim operating, and overturned the summary judgment decision. There is also a broad"equitable"discretion to stay or sever a counterclaim, depending on the nature of the main claim and the counterclaim, whether there isres judicata, During the three years'life of a suit, its defendant did not file a counterclaim.At the end of that period, the plaintiff tried to unilaterally discontinue the suit, but the defendant's right to counterclaim was remained. If a counterclaim is pled directly as a defence to the statement of claim, it cannot continue after summary judgment for the plaintiff;the two are inconsistent, and the chambers justice or applications judge must choose one. *Claiming Set-off*

BOOK_B.title: Status of counterclaim

commentary.text: Rule 3.58 See Alberta Rules of Court, Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.58. In Soler & Palau Canada Inc. v. Meyer's Sheet Metal Ltd., 2012 ABQB 496, 2012 CarswellAlta 1327, 545 A.R. 391, 77 Alta. L.R. (5th) 194 (Master), Master Hanebury said, at paragraph 47: 47 Rule 3.58 provides that a counterclaim is an independent action. It will not, in and of itself, prevent a plaintiff from obtaining summary judgment, unless the counterclaim constitutes a defence. A legal or equitable setoff, as defences, may prevent summary judgment. Procedural set-off does not.

BOOK_C.title: Status of counterclaim

commentary.text:
Rule 3.58 states that a counterclaim is an independent action. However, in practice although not reflected expressly in the , they are tied together more Rules of Court closely than two separate actions. Where there is a claim and counterclaim the parties hold concurrent questioning and set the matter down for trial concurrently, without the necessity of an order which would be required for two entirely separate actions. Omega Developments Inc. v. Canada Safeway Ltd., [2012] A.J. No. 967, 2012 ABQB 564 at para. 6 (Alta. Q.B. (Master)); see also, , [2016] A.J. No. 549, 2016 ABQB 172 WestJet v. ELS Marketing Inc. at para. 42 (Alta. Q.B.).
The settlement of the statement of claim or obtaining judgment on the statement of claim in an action does not settle or otherwise resolve the issues set out in the counterclaim which must be determined on their own. Richardson v. Richardson, [2018] A.J. No. 1177, 2018 ABCA 327 at para. 10 (Alta. C.A.). This is more important in the settlement context than the trial context, as the matters are usually heard at the same time.
One of the consequences of the counterclaim being an independent action is that a plaintiff might obtain summary judgment against the defendant on the plaintiff’s claim, even though the defendant’s counterclaim remains outstanding, Soler & Palau Canada Inc. v. Meyer’s Sheet Metal Ltd., [2012] A.J. No. 819, 2012 ABQB 496 at para. 47 (Alta. Q.B. (Master)); see also, , [2014] A.J. Bernum Petroleum Ltd. v. Birch Lake Energy Inc. No. 1199, 2014 ABQB 652 at para. 115 (Alta. Q.B.). or summary judgment on a counter- claim might be granted even though portions of the main claim must go to trial. Attila Dogan Construction and Installation Co. v. AMEC Americas Ltd., [2015] A.J. No. 1419,
